text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chickenpox (Varicella)

Thank you for the details; despite the normal blood work, the clustering of non-itchy papules on your abdomen, combined with your brother's recent chickenpox and the daycare exposure, strongly suggests early chickenpox. Given your immunizations are up-to-date, this may be a breakthrough infection or a viral variant. Do you observe any new lesions appearing today or tomorrow, and have you noticed any fever?
